summary: The claim and proof are mathematically sound. The supplied block aliases preserve the predecessor sets and successor maps, and the probability, reflected-mass, and moment normalizations agree with the supplied product fact. Parity exhausts the distinct reflected pairs, injectivity of the successor map gives exactly singleton or three-point rows, and the distinct pairs have disjoint endpoint sets even when centers overlap other endpoints. The cosh estimate therefore charges the weighted field variances to the original cubic endpoint masses and proves the uniform 2/3 estimate. The full-ambient halfspace argument correctly counts each noncentral reflection orbit twice and the central orbit once, giving the stated pointwise depth bound. Factoring the original target-law summands and applying Jensen and Cauchy-Schwarz then yields (1), and the cubic bound follows under that same original law. Singleton supports, empty sets of nontrivial rows, zero fields or variances, arbitrary differing widths and partitions, and lower-dimensional supports cause no gap. The weaker stated prefactor and exponent follow immediately from (1).
